articles.title: "Os prometo que a su niña no le va a faltar nunca de nada"
articles.standfirst: Historia MARCA de las horas más duras del tinerfeñismo. Una promesa entre lágrimas, un vestuario roto y un club y una ciudad que han demostrado que a la familia de Jesús de Miguel nunca la van a dejar sola
articles.summary: Historia MARCA de las horas más duras del tinerfeñismo. Una promesa entre lágrimas, un vestuario roto y un club y una ciudad que han demostrado que a la familia de Jesús de Miguel nunca la van a dejar sola
articles.body: Hay momentos en los que uno se queda sin saber muy bien qué escribir. Y lo que viví a la salida del tanatorio donde ya descansaba Jesús de Miguel antes del traslado fue uno de ellos. Rayco García, máximo accionista del CD Tenerife, reunió a toda la plantilla. Fue una reunión improvisada, de esas que surgen porque hay cosas que no pueden esperar. Había que explicarles cómo se iban a organizar las próximas horas, preparar la despedida de Jesús de Miguel como merece y, sobre todo, hablar de lo que viene. De cómo estar cerca de María y de su niña. Los jugadores le rodeaban. Le escuchaban. Y entonces llegó aquella última frase. "Os pido que estéis cerca de María… y yo os prometo que a su niña no le va a faltar nunca de nada". Rayco se rompió por completo. Empezó a llorar y se marchó. No pudo más. Y a quienes estábamos allí nos costó mucho no sentir que algo se nos rompía también por dentro. Porque no era una frase más. Era una promesa hecha desde el dolor, delante de un vestuario destrozado, pensando en una niña que acaba de perder a su padre. Me quedo con esa imagen. Con Rayco, con los futbolistas rodeándole y con esas palabras. También con la manera en la que el máximo accionista del Tenerife ha afrontado esta desgracia. Se ha puesto de escudo, ha dado la cara y ha atendido a todo el mundo desde el cariño, la cercanía y el respeto. Sin distancias. Entendiendo que, por encima de cualquier cargo, había una familia que necesitaba sentirse protegida. Y creo que eso también merece ser contado. Desde que conocimos la muerte de Jesús, he visto mucho dolor. Mucha incredulidad. Abrazos que no necesitaban palabras y personas que todavía no terminaban de creerse lo que había sucedido. He visto a un vestuario quedarse sin uno de los suyos, rotos de dolor, y a un club que ha sabido cuidar y arropar como pocos. Y Tenerife ha respondido de una manera que emociona. Su gente ha sentido esta pérdida como propia. Ha llorado a Jesús, ha abrazado a su familia y ha demostrado que todavía hay cosas que merecen la pena en una sociedad que tantas veces parece haber olvidado lo que significa ponerse en el lugar del otro. No importan los colores, ni de dónde viene cada uno, ni las diferencias. Cuando una familia sufre una desgracia así, lo único que importa es estar cerca. El CD Tenerife ha sido una familia para Jesús. Y ahora tiene que serlo, todavía más, para María y para su niña. Porque lo que viene es mucho más difícil de controlar. Ahora llegarán los días sin homenajes, sin cámaras, sin tanta gente alrededor. Los días en los que la vida seguirá para todos, pero no para quienes tienen que aprender a vivir con una ausencia. Y no hay nada más cruel que eso. Pero prefiero quedarme con lo vivido estos días. Con el dolor, sí, pero también con la enorme humanidad que he encontrado. Con un club que ha sabido arropar a los suyos y con una ciudad que ha demostrado cuánto puede querer. Por Demigol. Por María. Por su niña.

articles.title: As the SEC had four more teams in the initial CFP rankings than the Big Ten, Indiana's Curt Cignetti notes that 'the SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN'
articles.summary: The SEC had 10 teams in the first set of rankings while the Big Ten had six.
articles.body:
Indiana's Curt Cignetti continues to not be shy about poking the SEC.

Cignetti was asked Wednesday night on his weekly radio show about the season's first College Football Playoff rankings. No. 4 Indiana was the highest of six Big Ten teams in the initial top 25, while the SEC had 10 teams in the rankings.

Three of the six Big Ten teams were in the top 12. Five of the 10 SEC teams were in the top 12.

"Come on, these people — and there's a whole bunch of 'em — they march out of the tent and they're given instructions on what to say and they follow the company line, right?" Cignetti said when asked about the number of teams in the rankings between both conferences. "And I don't need to go any further."

It appears that Cignetti could be alluding to the CFP's TV contract with ESPN, the network that has the exclusive rights to every football game in the SEC. The Big Ten, meanwhile, doesn't have any games on ESPN, as its TV deal is with Fox, CBS and NBC.

But no one from ESPN has anything to do with the rankings. While ESPN's analysts are responsible for discussing the rankings when they're released on a weekly basis in November, the top 25 comes from the CFP's selection committee. That 12-person group includes Nebraska athletic director Troy Dannen, former Michigan State coach Mark Dantonio and former Nebraska coach Mike Riley.

"The SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN, you know, and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum," Cignetti also said. "So and that's why you see all these SEC teams up there, you know, some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high. But like I said, it's all gonna be played out on the field."

Ohio State is at No. 12 despite its win over Indiana because of its loss to No. 20 USC and the absence of starting quarterback Julian Sayin. Iowa is a spot ahead of the Trojans at No. 19. All three of those teams have two losses.

It's not new — or even unfair in certain aspects — to criticize the way that the SEC is discussed on ESPN's networks compared to other conferences. But it's also hard to allege a bias toward the SEC from a group of people that includes Big Ten influence as well as other committee members from conferences outside of the SEC.

And as Cignetti noted at the end of that second quote, the initial rankings are going to be irrelevant pretty soon. No. 20 USC travels to Indiana in two weeks. A third loss for the Trojans will eliminate them from the playoff conversation.

And Ohio State has No. 23 Oregon on Saturday along with games vs. Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan remaining. While those three teams may not be ranked, wins over all three (along with a victory over Oregon) will be enough to get the Buckeyes into the Big Ten title game and put them in a position to make the playoff.

articles.title: Radu: “Ahora tenemos que ir a la guerra por cada punto”
articles.standfirst: El meta cree que merecieron mejor suerte
articles.summary: El meta cree que merecieron mejor suerte
articles.body: Radu, que detuvo un penalti que mantuvo con vida al Celta hasta el final ante el USG (1-2), lamentó una nueva derrota europea de su equipo en Balaídos: “Hemos tenido muchas oportunidades para recuperar el partido. Tenemos que aprovechar más estas ocasiones porque ninguno nos regala nada”. Y lamentó el infortunio: “Tuvimos un poco de mala suerte en el segundo gol. El equipo ha hecho un buen segundo tiempo, también un buen primero, pero tenemos que aprovechar más las ocasiones que tenemos”. Y es consciente que deberán sumar muchos puntos en las cuatro jornadas que restan: “Ahora tenemos que ir a la guerra por cada punto, es la única opción que tenemos. Tenemos que ir a ganar cada partido que tenemos por delante. No tenemos otras opciones”, señaló el meta rumano. Sergio Carreira se expresó en los mismos términos: “Es verdad que hay cosas que corregir porque en las derrotas hay que corregirlas pero también creo que hay una base de un partido bueno para poder trabajar. Hay poco que achacarle al equipo hoy. Confío plenamente en el equipo y no dudo que lograremos los puntos necesarios”.

articles.title: Fabian Hürzeler: “El Coliseum tiene una energía única, ha sido una locura”
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Brighton analizaba al equipo azulón en la previa del partido de Conference
articles.summary: El técnico del Brighton analizaba al equipo azulón en la previa del partido de Conference
articles.body: Fabian Hürzeler comparecía en sala de prensa tras la victoria en el Coliseum frente al Getafe. El entrenador alemán tiene al equipo tercero en Premier y con pie y medio en la siguiente fase de la Conference League. Valoración: “Ha sido exactamente el partido que esperábamos, un partido defensivo, teníamos que tener paciencia. Tenemos que sacar las cosas positivas, es el tercer partido con puerta a cero. Estamos bien en la tabla y eso es lo que tenemos que sacar”. Puede hacer muchas cosas, puede atacar muy bien, lo hemos probado en Liga y aquí también. Estoy muy orgulloso por él por ese gol, siempre bastante pequeñito”. Automatismos del equipo: “Lo que creo es construir conexiones con los jugadores, no solo con los futbolistas, también con los seres humanos que hay detrás. Podemos construir relaciones diferentes, es muy importante la táctica y construir relaciones con ellos”. Verbruggen: “Es muy importante tener un arquero como el que tenemos, nos da seguridad a todo el equipo. Si hay una bola por ahí va a cogerla. No es solo un gran arquero, es un gran líder”. Dificultades del partido: “Intento no centrarme siempre en los resultados, ahora mismo tenemos buen nivel, pero lo queremos superior. Tenemos que continuar estando enfocados en dónde podemos mejorar. Este domingo tenemos un partido difícil contra...”. Ambiente en el Coliseum: “Al entrar al estadio, los caballos acompañándonos me sorprendió. Tiene una energía única y los aficionados transmiten emoción, es una locura”. Jugadores del Getafe: “Hay jugadores como Mangala, Gudelj y Mojica que me sorprenden mucho. El Getafe es un equipo que sabe cómo ganar y, sobre todo, en este magnífico ambiente”. El Getafe, con todo: “Siempre quiero jugar para marcar un gol más. Teníamos muchas ocasiones después del primer gol, el Getafe intentó atacar también, estuvimos ordenados y no sufrimos demasiado. Quiero siempre intentar marcar un gol más”.

images.caption: Fabian Hürzeler .

articles.title: Giráldez: “Creo que lo justo hubiese sido muestra victoria”
articles.standfirst: El técnico convencido de que superarán la fase de grupos
articles.summary: El técnico convencido de que superarán la fase de grupos
articles.body: Claudio Giráldez, tras la derrota 1-2 ante el USG, cree que su equipo merece más en Europa: “Hemos hecho cuatro buenos partidos en Europa, pero la realidad es que tenemos tres puntos pero la línea de los partidos de Europa es la que tenemos que mantener. La primera parte ha sido competida y en la segunda hemos sido muy superiores. Creo que ha sido un partido precioso. Creo que lo justo hubiese sido muestra victoria, en todo caso un empate, pero nos vamos de vacío”. Lamenta las ocasiones falladas: “Esto va de acertar y ellos lo han hecho, nosotros la hemos tenido para matarles con el 2-0 y luego para empatar en los últimos minutos y nos vamos de vacío”. No duda de que su equipo pasará la fase de grupos: “Estoy plenamente convencido que vamos a estar en la próxima ronda. Nos quedan cuatro partidos y no es normal que actuando así no consigamos puntos. Podemos ganar a los cuatro rivales que nos quedan y espero que todo el mundo lo vea de la misma manera y se sienta igual de orgulloso del equipo de lo que me siento yo”.

articles.title: 'He'll regret it': The day Alex Ferguson quit Aberdeen for Manchester United
articles.summary: It's 40 years since the legendary manager left the Dons after eight trophy-laden years.
articles.body:
When Alex Ferguson announced he was joining Manchester United after eight trophy-laden years at Aberdeen, there was shock among fans.

They had seen the legendary manager lead the Dons to three league titles, four Scottish Cups, the Cup Winners' Cup and the UEFA Super Cup.

One told BBC Scotland News at the time: "I think he's making the wrong move, I think he will regret it."

Ferguson went on to become one of the most successful football managers in history, winning 38 trophies during a 26-year tenure at Old Trafford.

On the 40th anniversary of Ferguson's decision to leave Aberdeen, some of those at the centre of the events have been reflecting on the day.

The story of Ferguson's defection to the English First Division on 6 November 1986 was broken by BBC Scotland football broadcaster Roddy Forsyth.

He had been tasked by his editor to head to Aberdeen to find out more about rumours that the Dons boss was in talks with Manchester United.

The flight he boarded in Glasgow was filled with journalists - but most were heading north to cover the Chinook helicopter disaster in Shetland in which 43 people died.

Once in Aberdeen, Forsyth eventually tracked Ferguson and the United chairman Martin Edwards down in an airport hotel.

He had called by chance asking to "speak to a Mr Edwards from Manchester".

The receptionist told him he was seated in the restaurant area.

"I heard some voices and made my way to them," Forsyth said.

"There was Martin Edwards and Alex Ferguson, and I said 'are you the new manager of Manchester United?' and he said 'yes'.

"They had a bottle of champagne which they were drinking and Fergie poured me a little champagne in a wine glass, and I toasted him as the new manager."

After a brief conversation, Forsyth got in touch with his newsroom confirming the story.

"Of course, the normal news led with the Sumburgh disaster, and then the sporting news led with Alex Ferguson," Forsyth added.

"It was a big day for news and sport and broadcasting.

"It was one of these utterly memorable days of your career and your life."

Ferguson had led the Scottish club to a period of success some fans thought would never end.

His departure was met with a mix of anger, disappointment, shock and acceptance.

The views of fans at the Pittodrie Bar were broadcast that day on BBC Reporting Scotland.

One was certain Ferguson would regret the move to the English giants.

"It is a sad case for Aberdeen, and I think he is making a wrong move," he said.

Another said: "Ferguson was preaching about having loyal players. He envied Rangers and Celtic for having that.

"In other words, he was condemning his players for leaving Aberdeen, he has set a perfect example he has just walked out."

Fast forward 40 years and fans today are generally a bit more measured on the whole episode.

Sandy Smith, 72, says he has "seen it all" in a lifetime of supporting the Dons.

"It was totally gutting," he said. "To be fair Man United and Aberdeen - there is no comparison.

"After all he did for the club, I was gutted.

"He had sticky first couple of seasons down there, but he got there in the end."

Ian Donald, the club's vice-chairman at the time, described it as a "shattering blow".

"It happened so quickly virtually overnight," he said in 1986.

"From yesterday morning perhaps having the best management team in Britain we are losing them both."

And it was a lot for the players to take in too.

Captain Willie Miller reflected on the time Ferguson left as a period of "uncertainty".

He thought all players missed the manager once he had gone, despite his famous temper.

"You would not get away with it now," he said.

"It was probably what we expected back then from a manager.

"I do not think the modern day player would accept anything close to it, you know, cups getting thrown around dressing rooms.

"He did not just want to win things, he wanted to win them with style. And it was OK with me.

"I was disappointed to see him go, I must admit, I think everybody was of the same opinion."

Ultimately, it was one man's choice to make and Ferguson made the move, taking his assistant with him.

In his first press conference as new boss he said: "I left probably the most secure job in British football with a life contract at Aberdeen.

"There's only one club that could possibly tempt me away from that and it is the only club I ever wanted to go to way from Aberdeen."

Thirteen Premier League titles, two Champions League victories, five FA cups and four League Cups later - maybe not.

articles.title: European Roundup: Woltemade & Baur deliver strong performances after Klopp snub, Rose's Bournemouth record seventh straight win, Hürzeler's Brighton yet to concede
articles.summary: German coaches Marco Rose and Fabian Hürzeler succeeded once again with their English clubs, while Nick Woltemade and Mika Baur delivered strong performances...
articles.body:
German coaches Marco Rose and Fabian Hürzeler succeeded once again with their English clubs, while Nick Woltemade and Mika Baur delivered strong performances after missing out from Germany's squad.

It wasn't all smooth sailing for Rose at the start of his Bournemouth reign, but the Cherries have extended their winning streak to seven games with a 3-1 win at Sparta Prague on Thursday evening. The visitors missed a first-half penalty-kick before securing a comeback win against their ten-man hosts.

USMNT international Tyler Adams scored in the European stage for the first time since his goal that helped RB Leipzig beat Atlético Madrid in the 2019/20 Champions League quarter-final round. Bournemouth are one of the three teams with a perfect Europa League record after four matchdays, alongside Benfica and Ferencváros, who stunned AC Milan with a 2-0 win at San Siro.

From 108 participating clubs, fellow Premier League side Brighton are the only team yet to concede a goal in UEFA competitions as they beat Getafe in Spain with Malick Yalcouye's solitary strike. Hürzeler's men sit in fifth place in the early standings, with Lugano, Panathinaikos, Twente and Monaco winning all their respective first three games in Conference League.

Baur and Woltemade unfazed by Germany snub

Germany U21 international Paris Brunner had his goal ruled out by VAR for an offside in Monaco's 2-0 win over FC Nordsjælland. The 20-year-old was a candidate for a first Germany call-up, but the name of the former BVB youngster wasn't found when Jürgen Klopp announced the squad earlier on Thursday.

Similarly, Baur and Woltemade helped their respective clubs to massive European wins after they failed to keep their spots in Germany's setup. Baur's Celtic recorded their first points in Europa League with an entertaining 3-2 win over Beşiktaş.

Woltemade once again started for Juventus as the Serie A outfit returned home with three points from AZ Alkmaar. The 24-year-old registered his fifth direct goal involvement of the competition, with an assist to former Eintracht Frankfurt striker Randal Kolo Muani in a 2-1 win for the visitors.

Marten Winkler is another German striker who has been performing well in Europe as he scored in back-to-back Europa League games for Anderlecht. Like the former Hertha BSC player, FC Midtjylland's Kjell Wätjen was a 2. Bundesliga midfielder last term with VfL Bochum.

However, the ex-Dortmund youth midfielder had a difficult night on Thursday as his first-half red card led to his club's 6-1 home defeat to Ajax. The historic Dutch side missed Julian Brandt due to an injury, but Germany's current first-choice goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen and Thilo Kehrer played the entire game.

articles.title: Thun 3-1 Hearts: Wouter Vrancken's side bruised by self-inflicted Conference League defeat
articles.summary: Report as Hearts lose 3-1 to Thun in the Conference League; Jamie McCart's own goal was the first of the errors; Stephen Kingsley gifted another; Stuart Findlay scored a late consolation; the Jambos have one point from their opening three games
articles.body:
Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish team were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley - who went off later with an injury - and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts are left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay - there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half - Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.

In the 20th minute McPake's effort from 25 yards after he had drifted in from the left had the power but was beaten away by the Thun 'keeper.

There appeared to be nothing untoward on the horizon but then came a Hearts horror show.

There was no real pressure on the Jambos goal when a long ball came into the box but with Lucien Dahler at his shoulder, a simple pass back from McCart somehow evaded Hearts 'keeper Beau Reus and slipped into the corner of the net.

Thun's second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.

Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.

The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but, three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later.

However, the 'keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.

On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.

The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott's header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.

Vrancken demands unity as Hearts seek to bounce back

"We have to stick together now. We know which situation we're in with all the circumstances.

"And there's only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard.

"In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?

"Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best.

"On the other hand, I'm still proud of what they did already in the run-up games."

articles.title: Big Ten conference commissioner gives tone deaf statement about 24-team College Football Playoff
articles.summary: Tony Petitti claims the 24-team college football playoff will make more games matter, but critics argue expanding the field strips regular-season stakes.
articles.body: If it feels like it's a ridiculous time to be a college football fan, that's because it is. While the AP Top 25 poll has become a running joke, at least fans can comfort themselves with the knowledge that it has little importance when it matters. Then the College Football Playoff selection committee released their poll this week and, well, to say it was indefensibly bad is a charitable overstatement. It's atrocious. It's humiliating. It's disgraceful. And it requires an entire overhaul of the selection committee process. WE NEED TO ABOLISH THE CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSMENT Don't worry though, because starting in 2027, the powers that be have voted to make more money and further remove what made college football special with a participation trophy 24-team playoff. This proposal had widespread support among many coaches who will now have greater job security, as well as some conference commissioners who have never actually watched or followed college football. Case in point? Big Ten conference commissioner Tony Petitti. COLLEGE FOOTBALL MOVES CLOSER TO 24-GAME PLAYOFF AND THE DESTRUCTION OF THE BEST REGULAR SEASON IN SPORTS Just this week, he defended the enlarged format with "logic" that is so disconnected from actual objective reality and history that it beggars belief. In an interview with College Sports Radio on Sirius XM, Petitti explained his "thinking" on the 24-team playoff coming next season and how it will impact the importance of games across the sport, week in and week out. "More games are going to matter," he said, inexplicably. "The way this format works is it’s got all different kinds of incentives, right? You’re going to fight like crazy to be inside the top 24, and then you want to get a home game, so you’re going to fight like crazy to be inside 16, and then you want to be inside eight, so you get a home game and a bye. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "So you’re always playing for something. There’s a lot at stake across all of this, and I think this year has just proven that trying to separate 12 teams from everybody else is just going to be incredibly difficult in the way college football is structured right now, and how tough it is to win the road. How the talent has kind of been more dispersed over many more programs, and then last thing is we just need to have give fans games that matter … I don’t think there’s any controversy in that at all." It's worth raising the question, do the people who run college football actually follow the sport? Has Petitti ever watched college football? Part of what makes it special and unique, as opposed to the NFL's regular season slog, is that the games actually matter. There are stakes, because the margin for error is so small. Expanding the playoff removes those stakes, particularly for the superconference teams and especially the SEC. This season, thanks to the selection committee's incompetence, we're already heading towards a three-loss SEC team, if not multiple three-loss teams, reaching the tournament. In a 24-team format, we'll have four-loss teams, if not five-loss SEC teams, reaching the top-24. Results are going to matter less than ever. In a roundabout way, this might actually help lead to more games between marquee opponents, specifically because the outcome doesn't matter. But claiming that fans will feel the same level of intensity, stakes, excitement and energy over fighting to be in the top-8 so they can get a bye? That's insanity. To be fair to Petitti, he did identify that home playoff games would be a big draw for fans. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER "So I think look, and then when you get to the playoff, you know fans are going to show up," Petitti said. "These on-campus games are one of the best parts about it. Going the 16 on-campus games is going to be absolutely great. You know, when fan bases get a home game, especially if that’s unexpected when the season started, you’re going to see incredible reactions across college football." We've already seen big programs struggle with attendance this year, outside marquee opponents. Just imagine how little interest there'll be in USC-Maryland or Miami-Stanford when the results don't mean anything. What makes all this even more frustrating is that everyone knows the actual motivation behind the playoff expansion: money. More playoff games means more high-value television properties to sell. The 24-team format ensures that programs from the Big Ten and SEC with large, passionate fanbases will have reasons to watch games, even when they're 6–4. It's rewarding mediocrity in search of more financial rewards. Which is what college football has become in recent years.

The No. 23 Ducks are coming off a confidence-boosting win over Northwestern, heading on the road to face No. 12 Ohio State (6-2, 4-1) this Saturday. That matchup originally included the preseason Nos. 1 and 2 teams in the AP poll.

But in this chaotic college football season, the Buckeyes are reeling after a road loss to No. 20 USC.

Other Big Ten teams in this week's CFP rankings include No. 19 Iowa, No. 8 UCLA and No. 4 Indiana.

articles.title: Celtic 3-2 Besiktas: Duran & Osmand spark Celtic into life - but where does that leave Hogh?
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill has previously said he is unsure of his best team, but it is now obvious that Camilo Duran is Celtic's best option through the middle.
articles.body:
With an hour gone at Parkhead on Thursday, hope in the stands was in short supply.

Celtic were 1-0 down against Besiktas and heading towards a fourth straight defeat in this season's Europa League.

Manager Martin O'Neill turned to his bench for a spark, bringing on Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran to replace Sebastian Tounekti and James Forrest out wide.

Osmand's first touch nestled in the bottom corner of Alexander Nubel's goal, just 43 seconds after the 20-year-old attacker came on.

All of a sudden, Celtic had a threat in behind and Besiktas looked rattled.

Then, on 77 minutes, O'Neill withdrew Kasper Hogh after another underwhelming display from the club record signing and moved Duran through the middle.

Osmand played Duran through with a delightful pass and the Colombian rounded Nubel before slotting Celtic into the lead.

Orkun Kokcu levelled for Besiktas with a fine strike, but Duran had the final say two minutes later, controlling Kieran Tierney's scuffed shot and beating Nubel from close range to send the home support into ecstasy.

Late Duran double downs Besiktas to give Celtic first Europa League win

Latest Celtic news, analysis and fan views

"Everything changed with the subs; Osmand coming on and Duran going through the middle," former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov said on TNT Sports. "They freed up space for Nygren and Baur. It was a really positive 30 minutes."

Not since Johannes Edvaldsson against Jeunesse d'Esch in the European Cup in September 1977 had a Celtic substitute scored twice in Europe (excluding qualifiers).

"Osmand came on, first touch put the ball in the net and that's really difficult, he can definitely score a goal. Duran has been fabulous for us all season no matter where he plays," O'Neill said of his goalscorers.

The Northern Irishman was asked whether it was a case of inspired substitutions or rather evidence that he should have started his best players.

"I'm not standing up for myself, not at all," he said.

"It was in design to do exactly what it did. We've played nine games in 25 days, some players needed a breather and you can get re-energised from coming on the field.

"I'm going to say that that was our plan and those players were going to come on the pitch at some point in the game."

The contrast between Celtic's attacking play with Hogh leading the line and with Duran through the middle was stark.

The £11m Dane's effort cannot be questioned. He continued to battle to try to make things happen, but since arriving from Bodo/Glimt in the summer, he has now failed to score in 16 of his 17 Celtic appearances.

In 77 minutes against Besiktas, he didn't have a single shot and managed just one touch in the opposition box.

Duran, meanwhile, played just half an hour and scored two goals, had two shots, and registered four touches in the Besiktas box.

O'Neill has previously said he is unsure of his best team, but it is now obvious that Duran is Celtic's best option through the middle.

Despite Hogh's price tag, it feels inevitable he will be among the Celtic substitutes for high-stakes games.

"It'll be tough for Hogh," Hearts defender Craig Halkett said on TNT Sports. "He was the big-money singing but it's not coming off for him.

"As a player you need to keep your head down, keep working hard and hope it turns."

Osmand too appears to have pushed himself to the front of the queue to start off the left. The former Fulham man is direct and evidently has an eye for goal, with a happy knack for scoring in big games.

"This is a great team we're playing against," Osmand told TNT Sports. "Camilo [Duran] did amazing, he's such a poacher. Credit to him.

"It's a lot harder starting games. The team dug in, stayed strong and we got our rewards.

"[The goal] caught me off guard, but I'm just glad I caught it nice. I just want to come on and make something happen. So happy with tonight."

articles.title: Feijóo: "Si la final del Mundial 2030 no es en España deberíamos retirarnos de la organización"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del PP lo tiene muy claro
articles.summary: El presidente del PP lo tiene muy claro
articles.body: Alberto Núñez Feijóo, presidente del Partido Popular y candidato a las elecciones generales del próximo domingo 29 de noviembre, lo tiene claro. En palabras a 'El Chiringuito', el gallego tiene en sus planes lanzar un órdago a la FIFA si acaba convirtiéndose en presidente del Gobierno: si la final del Mundial 2030 no se juega en España, abogaría por retirarse de la organización del evento. Feijóo no dudó cuando se le preguntó al respecto y dio tres motivos por los que España debería ser el país donde se jugase el último de los partidos del próximo Mundial, la gran joya del mayor evento futbolístico del planeta: "¿Dónde debe ser la final del Mundial 2030? Donde es lo justo y lo oportuno, donde es indiscutible, en España. Primero, porque España es capaz de organizar cualquier evento deportivo con éxito, lo hemos demostrado. Segundo, porque España y Portugal fueron la sede de la organización del Mundial de fútbol y, posteriormente, se invitó a Marruecos. Tercero, porque España es la primera potencia del mundo y la campeona del mundo en el último Mundial masculino y también femenino". El presidente del PP tiene claro el que sería su discurso ante la FIFA si gana las elecciones: "España ha de organizar la final de la Copa del Mundo. Y, si no la organiza, en mi opinión, España no debería participar en la organización del Mundial". Al ser preguntado directamente por si se diese el caso de llegar a La Moncloa y Marruecos nos quitase ese partido, Feijóo abogaría porque España retirase directamente la candidatura: "Sí, la respuesta es, sí", respondió de forma tajante.

articles.title: Japan’s former soccer chief aims to run against Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency
articles.summary: Japan Football Association Honorary President Kozo Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run for the FIFA presidency in next March’s election, becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football’s top job.
articles.body: Japan Football Association Honorary President Kozo Tashima announced on Thursday that he intended to run for the FIFA presidency in next March’s election, becoming the first Japanese candidate to seek world football’s top job. The 68-year-old former Japan forward has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and became JFA president the following year. Tsuneyasu Miyamoto succeeded him as JFA chief in 2024. “I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the JFA,” Tashima told reporters after a JFA board meeting in Tokyo. “It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. “What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.” Nippon Sports said Tashima still needs nominations from five national associations, which is required to stand for election. He is expected to get support from some Southeast Asian countries and European associations critical of incumbent Gianni Infantino. Potential candidates have until November 18 to submit their nominations. Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first candidate to publicly declare his intention to challenge Infantino when he announced in October that he would stand in the FIFA presidential election against his fellow Swiss. Infantino has faced opposition since his unsuccessful attempt in July to bring private investors into a new FIFA commercial entity holding rights linked to competitions including the World Cup. However, the 56-year-old administrator’s prospects of securing another term received a significant boost last month after the head of Asian football endorsed his bid. Support across FIFA’s confederations has left him in a commanding position among the organisation’s 211 voting members.

articles.title: Arch Manning Compared to Trevor Lawrence By Todd McShay Despite Texas QB's NFL Draft Stock Slide
articles.summary: The Ringer's Todd McShay feels Texas quarterback Arch Manning could follow a similar trajectory to the Jacksonville Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence on his way to finding eventual success in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Ringer's Todd McShay feels Texas quarterback Arch Manning could follow a similar trajectory to the Jacksonville Jaguars' Trevor Lawrence on his way to finding eventual success in the NFL.

"Trevor Lawrence left Clemson, similar skillset, physical tools... five years later, three different systems, it finally started to click last year and this year," McShay said around the 8:10 mark of Thursday's episode of The Rich Eisen Show.

McShay added, "Just because Arch isn't ready right now doesn't mean he can't get there."

Manning has struggled with inconsistency during his second year as a full-time starter for Texas, which came in at No. 7 on the first CFP selection committee rankings after a 6-2 start to the season.

McShay said Lawrence played in a "simple" Clemson offense that leaned heavily on big receivers making plays before finding his fit in the NFL.

"I'd like to see, if Arch doesn't go back to Texas... maybe getting with the right person and the right system to help his development could help," McShay said. "I also watch [head coach Steve Sarkisian]'s offense and I say the play-calling is where I have the issue."

McShay continued, "I don't think Arch has a lot of power pre-snap. I don't see him in control of this offense. He is a joystick, at times, for Sark's brilliance... I think sometimes we forget these guys need to develop."

By the time Lawrence entered the 2021 NFL draft, he was a lock as the top overall pick. ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr. ranked Lawrence at the time as one of his top 10 quarterback prospects of all time.

In his most recent 2027 NFL draft big board, Kiper ranked Manning as the sixth-best quarterback in the upcoming class behind Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker, Miami's Darian Mensah, Notre Dame's CJ Carr, Ole MIss' Trinidad Chambliss and Missouri's Austin Simmons.

Kiper noted Manning has "the size, mobility and arm strength that NFL teams look for in a franchise quarterback," but added the 22-year-old is "too inconsistent, especially when it comes to accuracy and decision-making."

Manning will get his next chance to prove he has continued developing his ability to read opposing defenses when the Longhorns head north for a Saturday matchup at No. 19 Missouri.

articles.title: From Siu to see you: Cristiano Ronaldo says goodbye to international football
articles.summary: The iconic 'Siu' celebration will no longer ring out on the international stage.
articles.body: The iconic 'Siu' celebration will no longer ring out on the international stage. Not all curtain calls are happy spectacles, a packed arena cheering the last hurrah of a performer par excellence. Cristiano Ronaldo had his floodlit moments in the cauldrons of Stade de France, Porto, Gelsenkirchen, Luzhniki, Wembley, the Bernabeu or Munich's Allianz Arena.On Thursday, Portugal's superstar announced his intention to retire from the country's national team in a social media post, bringing an end to one of the most illustrious careers in all football history. "The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team," he wrote in an 866-word message. "I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world."Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future ... A journey that began in Aug 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end. When I look back at everything with the national team, I don't just see the matches, goals, records or trophies."All expected him to say ‘obrigado’ at Dallas Stadium after Portugal lost to Spain in his last World Cup match on July 6, 2026. It marked his 27th appearance across a record six tournaments (2006-2026), making him the oldest player in a World Cup knockout match at 41.Instead, the Portugal great, if not the greatest, waited for his bete noire Lionel Messi to sail into the twilight at the Monumental Stadium, waited till national coach Jorge Jesus’ royal ignore forced him into an ugly spat, a chase to the airport to coax him back. Of late, Cristiano had been making headlines for the wrong reasons.Images of Cristiano struggling inside the rival penalty box have long overshadowed his overwhelming prowess that made him snatch five Ballons D’Or to Messi’s eight. Their game of one-upmanship spread across two decades leaving the world gasping for more. Gen Z is cleaved down the middle over the Portuguese and the Argentinian. The discourse will take some years to lose steam.No men’s footballer has made as many international appearances (234) or scored as many goals (146) for their nation as Ronaldo. As a testament to his longevity — 94 of them came after his 30th birthday.The five-time Ballon d’Or-winner made his international debut in 2003, and won the 2016 European Championship, in addition to two Nations League titles, with Portugal.Ronaldo scored three goals at this summer’s World Cup as his nation exited in the Round of 16.Recalling his great matches would be an exercise in academic drudgery. The hat-trick against Spain in Sochi in 2018 and the World Cup qualifier goals against Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s Sweden in 2013 are just the tip of the iceberg.So are the moments of irony. In 2012, Luis Nani missed one on a platter offered to him by Cristiano in the Euro semifinal against Spain. Portugal lost. Four years later, Cristiano’s final against France ended in a tear-soaked heartache, injured and substituted after 25 minutes. Portugal went on to win their first continental title.Before Ronaldo, a senior Portugal side had never won anything, had only made the World Cup semifinals twice, in 1966 and 2006 (his first World Cup). With him leading them, they won three trophies in nine years.Madeira, his birthplace, has a museum as a tribute to its most famous son. Like Santos has one for Pele.Accolades will continue to flow and the ‘Siuuu’ celebration will be replicated by boys across the globe for years to come.For now, like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and currently sits on 985. The immortal longings refuse to die.As his goodbye post reads: “Goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people’s hearts.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: India's near-perfect start to their SAFF Championship campaign was soured by two goals they conceded in stoppage time as the defending champions outwitted Pakistan 3-2 in their group B opener at National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday.Coach Naushad Moosa had just 17 players to choose from, two of them goalkeepers, as clubs were reluctant to release players when they have ISL duties. But a reserve side that trained just twice before the opener turned pre-match predictions on its head, scoring twice inside the first 20 minutes. Both goals came from the boots of Suhail Ahmad Bhat, while Manglenthang Kipgen made it 3-0 in the first half.With such a big advantage, it was understandable that complacency would be India's biggest enemy. Moosa could even afford to try out new players, but the mood soured in stoppage time as Pakistan struck twice through Najeeb Ullah and Alamgir Ghazi.India are defending their SAFF Championship title with a reserve side. The seniors will travel to New Zealand next week for two friendlies with the World Cuppers.In Dhaka, however, Moosa's side played on the front foot, taking Pakistan by surprise.Bhat thought he had opened India's account with a nice grounder, but the goal was wrongly ruled offside. Television replays showed the Bagan striker had beat the trap before scoring.The forward, however, was not to be denied for long. Two minutes later, Muhammad Suhail ran to catch a quick throw-in from Muhammad Uvais and then delivered an inch-perfect ball into the penalty area, where Bhat turned it home.Bhat's second came through another perfect through ball, this time from midfielder Abhishek Suryavanshi. articles.summary: "Invité a Florentino Pérez para que pueda ir a Honduras. Hablamos del tema de construcción, porque Honduras viene con bastantes proyectos de construcción de carreteras y otras obras"
articles.body: El presidente hondureño, Nasry 'Tito' Asfura, quien concluyó su visita a España, donde asistió a la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana, invitó al titular del Real Madrid, Florentino Pérez, a que visite Honduras para que conozca las oportunidades que ofrece a la inversión en obras de infraestructura. "Lo invité para que pueda ir a Honduras. Hablamos del tema de construcción, porque Honduras viene con bastantes proyectos de construcción de carreteras y otras obras, y si estuviese interesado en invertir en Honduras", dijo Asfura, resalta un comunicado de la Casa Presidencial en Tegucigalpa. El gobernante calificó la reunión con el presidente del Real Madrid como "una experiencia positiva" en la que además se habló "sobre el desarrollo del fútbol y las oportunidades de ampliar la presencia de las academias deportivas vinculadas al club -español- en Honduras". Asfura y Pérez también dialogaron de la posibilidad de fortalecer los programas formativos en materia de fútbol a partir de 2027, mediante un convenio entre el Real Madrid y una empresa hondureña para el desarrollo de academias en el país. Aunque no hubo ningún compromiso sobre inversión confirmado, el presidente hondureño resaltó la apertura mostrada por Pérez durante el encuentro y la importancia de continuar acercamientos para proyectar las oportunidades que ofrece Honduras. Asfura, empresario de la construcción, también expresó su admiración por la remodelación que ha tenido el Estadio Santiago Bernabéu, en el que hubo un intercambio de camisetas con Pérez. El gobernante centroamericano le obsequió a Pérez una camiseta de la selección de Honduras, en azul y blanco, con el número 10 y el nombre de Florentino Flores, mientras que el presidente del club español hizo lo mismo entregándole una del Real Madrid, con el número 1 en la espalda y su nombre, Nasry Asfura. Asfura también recibió una camiseta autografiada del delantero del Real Madrid Kyliam Mbappé, lo que también le emocionó.

articles.title: 53 red cards in one match! Brazil football game sets bizarre world record after mass brawl
articles.summary: Football witnessed an extraordinary scene in Brazil after a mass brawl during an under-20s match resulted in 53 dismissals, setting a new world record for
articles.body: Football witnessed an extraordinary scene in Brazil after a mass brawl during an under-20s match resulted in 53 dismissals, setting a new world record for the most red cards issued in a single game.The unprecedented incident took place during a local U20 semifinal in Minas Gerais on Sunday, when Mamoré were leading Uberlândia 3-1 in the second half. Celebrations following Mamoré's third goal triggered a confrontation that soon escalated into a mass fight involving players and officials from both sides.According to the referee's report, Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto sent off 40 players and eight members of the coaching and support staff in the aftermath of the brawl. Three players had already received red cards earlier in the contest. Two Uberlândia board members were also dismissed, taking the overall tally to 53.The figure surpasses the previous Guinness World Record of 36 red cards, set during an Argentinian fifth-division fixture between Atlético Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in February 2011.The referee's report provided details of how the chaotic scenes unfolded. Mamoré player Davi allegedly taunted the opposition bench while celebrating his team's third goal, prompting Uberlândia goalkeeping coach Paulo Sérgio Dias Dos Santos to enter the pitch and confront him.What followed was a widespread altercation involving players and members of the staff, leaving the referee with little choice but to take disciplinary action against those involved.The situation also reportedly took a threatening turn, with Drosghic Modesto alleging that several individuals directed death threats and other threats of violence towards him. A police report was subsequently filed in connection with the incident, according to the referee's account.The match was stopped for 40 minutes before eventually being abandoned as the situation could not be brought under control.The trouble did not end with the on-field confrontation. Following the match, allegations emerged that Uberlândia officials had damaged equipment belonging to Mamoré. Members of the Mamoré team were also accused of vandalising the home dressing room.The incident has now set a remarkable new benchmark in football's disciplinary history, with the 53 dismissals eclipsing the previous record by a considerable margin.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: Lista de España para cerrar el glorioso 2026 ante Chequia e Inglaterra
articles.summary: Lista de España para cerrar el glorioso 2026 ante Chequia e Inglaterra
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente desvela este viernes la última lista de convocados de 2026, el año de la segunda estrella. Lo hará a las 11.30 horas, con el recuerdo a las víctimas del terrible accidente de tren de Urda y a Jesús de Miguel. Será en el estadio Metropolitano, donde el domingo 15 se decidirá si España o Inglaterra pasan como primeras de grupo a los cuartos de final de la Liga de las Naciones. Eso da derecho a jugar la vuelta en casa. Antes, el jueves, la campeona del mundo se medirá a la Chequia de Santi Denia en Praga. El cierre del curso viene marcado por dos bajas importantes respecto al equipo base del Mundial. Son las de Rodri y Dani Olmo, a las que se suma la de Eric García. La otra cara de la moneda es el regreso de dos ausentes por lesión hace un mes: Joan García y Pedro Porro. La baja de Rodri devuelve a España al tiempo en que su ahora capitán estuvo de baja a causa de la grave lesión de rodilla que sufrió en septiembre de 2024 y sus secuelas. Entonces, con una versión excelente de Zubimendi, la selección ganó ocho partidos y empató tres. Pero aquel era un Zubimendi pletórico, primero en la Real y después en el Arsenal. El de hoy es un jugador que fue noticia este miércoles porque, por primera vez esta temporada, fue titular en un partido de Premier o de Champions. La fe que tiene De la Fuente en el donostiarra está fuera de todo debate: “Tenemos al mejor mediocentro del mundo, Rodri, y al segundo mejor, Zubimendi”. Así que por ahí las dudas son pocas. Donde se abre una plaza es en el acompañante de Martín. Después de mucho tiempo, Pablo Barrios está sano para ir a la selección. La de pivote es una de las posiciones que puede ocupar el rojiblanco. A su lado aparecen Luis Milla, motor del exuberante Como de Cesc, y Chema Andrés, el pivote de la Sub 21 y del no menos sorprendente Brighton. Las bajas obligan al seleccionador a sacudir el árbol. En la zaga cotiza al alza Jacobo Ramón, el mejor central de lo que va de temporada en la Serie A. Como muchos de los baluartes de la Sub 21, está pendiente de que su club le dé permiso o no para ir al Europeo. Esa vía lleva a Pubill al lateral derecho como pareja de Pedro Porro. El sacrificado sería Fresneda, mientras que Le Normand, llamado de urgencia tras la lesión de Eric, queda en la recámara. En la zona de Dani Olmo el abanico de opciones es amplio: Isco, Gabri Veiga, Fornals, Moleiro, Yeremay... La desaparición de Gavi de los planes de Flick ya hizo que en la lista para la larga ventana de septiembre y octubre el campeón del mundo se quedara fuera. Es una zona en la que también puede entrar Barrios, aunque su perfil se aleje del tipo de jugador que es Olmo. En la Final Four de 2025, De la Fuente recuperó a Isco, pero esa apuesta se vio anegada por las lesiones. Ahora el bético, a sus 34 años, vuelve a marcar diferencias y a llamar a una puerta en la que la competencia es voraz. Y, una vez más, la del tercer delantero centro es una posición con interrogantes. En la última lista se cayó Borja Iglesias (además está lesionado), y entraron Roberto Fernández y Carlos Espí. En esta ocasión, De la Fuente ya puede contar con Samu Aghehowa, ya recuperado de la rotura del cruzado sufrida en enero. Es el perfil de delantero más transgresor, una variante radicalmente distinta a las demás. En todo.

articles.title: Alicia de la Cuerda ya tiene su pinche oportunidad: "Mi corazoncito siempre ha sido blanco"
articles.standfirst: La toledana ha pasado de ser capitana del filial del Real Madrid a ser una de las grandes esperanzas de Cruz Azul
articles.summary: La toledana ha pasado de ser capitana del filial del Real Madrid a ser una de las grandes esperanzas de Cruz Azul
articles.body: Alicia de la Cuerda sorprendió a propios y extraños al pasar del filial del Real Madrid -donde era capitana- a firmar por el Cruz Azul, equipo mexicano con el que se ha ligado hasta 2029. "Pensé que era momento de vivir una experiencia diferente. Cuando se me presentó la oportunidad y me mostraron el proyecto y la confianza que tenían en mí, creí que debía dar el salto", asegura en MARCA la protagonista. "Pensé que me iba a costar adaptarme más, pero aquí la gente es adorable y me han ayudado con todo, así que estoy agradecida y súper contenta", añade. Natural de Toledo, Alicia comenzó a jugar al fútbol en las Escuelas Deportivas Municipales de Argés. "Mis padres -Helena y Javier- cuentan que no sabía andar y ya estaba pegada al balón", cuenta Alicia entre risas. "Mi padre jugaba al fútbol (sala) y siempre que iba a verle jugar me bajaba al parqué y me ponía a darle patadas", añade. A los nueve años fichó por el Atlético de Madrid, y, tras ocho temporadas de rojiblanca acabó firmando por el Real Madrid. "El Atlético es un club maravilloso que siempre me ha tratado maravillosamente, pero mi corazoncito siempre ha sido blanco. Cuando tuve la oportunidad de irme al Real Madrid lo vi como la opción de cumplir un sueño y así lo viví mientras estuve allí", destaca. A pesar de su calidad y su polivalencia (puede actuar como centrocampista o en posiciones más retrasadas), De la Cuerda no gozó de oportunidades en el primer equipo. "Todas las jugadoras somos ambiciosas y siempre queremos más. El Real Madrid es un club con mucha competencia y me alegro mucho por las compañeras que sí han podido llegar", apunta Alicia, que, cansada, decidió buscar fuera lo que no le daban en casa. "Salir de mi zona de confort es algo que me va a ayudar a crecer como futbolista y como persona. Quiero seguir creciendo, mejorar y nunca se sabe si en un futuro podré tener esa oportunidad. Nunca me cierro puertas. Ahora estoy centrada en Cruz Azul, pero siempre estaré agradecida al Real Madrid", sentencia. Alicia es la primera futbolista española en vestir la camiseta de Cruz Azul. O será, ya a la semana de aterrizar en Ciudad de México sufrió una rotura muscular en el gemelo y sóleo de la pierna derecha que le ha impedido debutar hasta la fecha. "Fue un pequeño revés, pero las compañeras me lo están haciendo más llevadero", asegura la toledana, que cita a Solis Ofelia, Mia León o Daniela García como sus madrinas en el equipo. "Tengo ganas de estar recuperada al 100% y poder aportar al equipo desde dentro del campo", recalca quien lucirá el 10 y su apellido (De la Cuerda) a la espalda. Además, ya sabe la novatada que se cobrarán sus compañeras. "Me han dicho que les tengo que hacer una tortilla de patatas, pero de momento me resisto", confiesa. Cruz Azul cerrará la fase de grupos del Apertura 2026 sin opción de clasificarse para los play-off por el título, así que la vista está en el siguiente torneo. "Cruz Azul es un club con amplia trayectoria y que va creciendo y apostando cada vez más por el fútbol femenino. Creo que a medio plazo podemos dar de qué hablar", asegura Alicia. "La Liga MX cada vez tiene más españolas y eso también se agradece. Me apetece enfrentarme a ellas y poder charlar un rato en el campo", añade. El cambio de vida para Alicia ha sido pleno al vivir sola por primera vez en un país diferente y con una cultura y gastronomía diversa. "Los primeros días llamaba a mi madre para que me ayudara con las cosas de la casa, pero ya me manejo. Cuando voy a comer a un restaurante he aprendido a preguntar por el picante porque para lo que ellos no pica para nosotros sí. ¡Ya me he llevado algún susto! Al principio también me costó entenderles bien porque tiene muchas palabras y expresiones diferentes, pero ahora ya lo hago sin problema", exclama 'La española', apodo que le han puesto en el vestuario. La saga De la Cuerda-García-Calvo continúa con Claudia, hermana de Alicia tres años menor que ella y actualmente jugadora del Real Madrid B [ella sí ha debutado ya con el primer equipo]. "La echo muchísimo de menos. Coincidir con ella en el mismo equipo ha sido maravilloso y nos ha unido más. Tener ese apoyo, la confianza para decirle cualquier cosa... Ojalá pronto volvamos a coincidir", asegura. ¿Quién es mejor? "Somos dos perfiles diferentes", regatea con clase Alicia.

articles.title: De Roma a Atenas: vuelve el gen de las remontadas
articles.standfirst: El Madrid de Mourinho remontó un 3-1 en Roma y un 2-1 en Atenas, y rompió tres empates en los minutos finales; solo Betis y Atlético frenaron esa pólvora
articles.summary: El Madrid de Mourinho remontó un 3-1 en Roma y un 2-1 en Atenas, y rompió tres empates en los minutos finales; solo Betis y Atlético frenaron esa pólvora
articles.body: Caminar por el alambre vuelve a resultarle natural al Real Madrid. En un curso que apenas arranca, el equipo de Mourinho ha recuperado esa testarudez que aflora cuando el marcador se le pone cuesta arriba, un reflejo que el madridismo daba por extraviado tras dos temporadas viendo a los suyos encajar el golpe sin saber devolverlo. En el Madrid, volver a la vida ya es una tradición. Lo singular es el escenario. El fenómeno no habita el Bernabéu, templo natural de las noches imposibles, sino lejos de Chamartín. El conjunto blanco ha aprendido a sublevarse de visitante, y lo ha hecho por partida doble en su competición fetiche, la Champions, donde el madridismo guarda sus mejores recuerdos de rebeldía. Roma y Atenas, dos capitales que inventaron buena parte del mundo, le han servido para reencontrarse con su vena heroica, la de los finales escritos contra pronóstico. En el Olímpico levantó un 3-1 a golpe de banquillo: Mourinho removió el avispero con sus cambios e inoculó una convicción que ha perdurado en forma de siete victorias consecutivas. La última, en el Allwyn Arena, repitió el libreto hasta en los detalles. Hombres salidos del banco —Endrick agitando la banda y Valverde rematando con un zapatazo desde la frontal— le dieron al equipo la corriente que le faltaba para firmar el 2-3. El propio técnico explicó esa doble resurrección europea tras el partido: “En los dos momentos críticos hemos sabido reaccionar y tener personalidad”. No todas las resurrecciones nacieron de ir por detrás. El Madrid también ha sabido quebrar la igualada lejos de casa, en esos duelos donde el rival creía tener el terreno nivelado y asomaba, sobre la bocina, ese ADN. Pasó en Cornellà-El Prat en la primera jornada, con Espí desnivelando ante el Espanyol. Se repitió en Elche, otra vez con la rúbrica del delantero en los compases finales. Y ocurrió en el Camp Nou, donde el empate a uno se rompió en la recta final por medio de Mbappé para un 1-2 que, más allá de los tres puntos, enderezó el ánimo de todo el proyecto. Aquel Clásico fue el verdadero punto de inflexión del curso. Existe cierto contraste con el carácter de la campaña pasada. En toda la temporada 2025-26, el Madrid de Xabi Alonso y Arbeloa apenas firmó dos reacciones de este tipo, y ambas sobre la bocina. La primera, en el Bernabéu ante el Rayo (2-1), resuelta con un penalti de Mbappé en el minuto 90+10 después de que De Frutos hubiera igualado el tanto inicial de Vinicius. La segunda, en Balaídos (1-2), con un zapatazo de Valverde en el 90+4 que coronó la remontada tras el empate de Borja Iglesias. Dos golpes de autoridad en un curso entero. Con el calendario doblando la esquina de noviembre, el Madrid de Mourinho ya iguala esa cifra. Dos manchas, sin embargo, ensombrecen el cuadro. La Cartuja y el Metropolitano, o lo que es lo mismo, Betis y Atlético, son los escenarios donde esa pólvora no prendió. Ante los verdiblancos el Madrid trenzó buen fútbol, pero no lo tradujo en gol, y el penalti errado por Mbappé terminó condenándolo a una derrota temprana. En el derbi madrileño ocurrió lo contrario: los de Mourinho no exhibieron sus mejores galas ofensivas, resistieron incluso con un hombre menos tras la justa expulsión de Huijsen y un coletazo postrero apenas maquilló un partido marcado por una polémica arbitral que, a juicio del club blanco, condicionó el marcador en su contra. Dos vuelcos de visitante, tres empates rotos sobre la bocina y siete triunfos encadenados. Juanito juraba que los 90 minuti en el Bernabéu eran molto longo. Este Madrid ha exportado la sentencia. Ahora también lo están siendo lejos de casa. Mourinho mueve el banco y todo ello tiene su efecto en el marcador.

articles.title: Rafa Nadal y la presidencia del Madrid: qué necesita y qué cambia con su entrada en la Junta
articles.standfirst: La posibilidad de que sea algún día el sucesor de Florentino gana peso con este movimiento
articles.summary: La posibilidad de que sea algún día el sucesor de Florentino gana peso con este movimiento
articles.body: La incorporación de Rafa Nadal a la junta directiva del Real Madrid vuelve a situar su nombre en el debate sobre el futuro de la presidencia. El club anunció el 4 de noviembre que someterá su nombramiento a la ratificación de la Asamblea General de Socios Compromisarios que se celebrará el próximo sábado 21 de noviembre. Es un paso importante tanto del Real Madrid como de Rafa, aunque no supone que haya sido elegido como sucesor de Florentino Pérez. El hermetismo en este sentido tanto en el club blanco como en el entorno de Rafa es total. Por ahora, la leyenda del tenis formará parte del club sin hacer más ruido que el que su planetaria figura genera por sí solo. Su madridismo, su reconocimiento internacional y el respeto que genera su trayectoria ayudan a entender por qué aparece en las conversaciones sobre la presidencia. Ganador de 22 Grand Slam y de dos oros olímpicos, Nadal es una figura conocida en todo el mundo y su unión con el club más laureado de la historia convierte este movimiento en una jugada maestra y de dimensión mundial. La entrada en la directiva le permitirá, tal y como aseguró el propio Rafa, conocer desde dentro el funcionamiento del club y adquirir experiencia en su gestión. El propio Real Madrid destacó en su comunicado "su competitividad, su compromiso y su respeto a los rivales como motivos para incorporarlo". Quienes conocen bien a Nadal aseguran que no da este paso para estar de brazos cruzados, sino para aportar en todo lo que pueda. Para encabezar una candidatura hay requisitos concretos. El artículo 40 de los estatutos exige 20 años ininterrumpidos como socio para optar a presidente, 15 para vicepresidente y 10 para el resto de la junta. La candidatura debe presentar, además, un preaval bancario de al menos el 15% del presupuesto de gastos, respaldado por el patrimonio personal de sus integrantes. Nadal es socio de honor desde 2011, número 67.778. Si su antigüedad reconocida parte de ese año, alcanzaría los 20 años en 2031. Su llegada a la junta abre también otra posibilidad prevista en los estatutos: si la presidencia queda vacante de forma definitiva, los directivos eligen a uno de sus miembros y la Asamblea debe ratificarlo. Esa vía existe, aunque el texto no dice que baste con tener 15 años de socio para utilizarla. El tenista nunca ha ocultado que el cargo le atrae, pero ha evitado presentarlo como un objetivo decidido. En 2024, en una entrevista con Ana Pastor en El Objetivo de LaSexta, lo explicó con claridad: "Claro que me haría ilusión pero no lo tengo en mi plan de vida". Dejó abierta la posibilidad de planteárselo si algún día se daban las circunstancias. Más recientemente, en mayo de 2026, se desmarcó de las informaciones que lo vinculaban con una candidatura de Enrique Riquelme, con el que mantiene una buena relación y que ayer le tendió la mano. Expresó su respeto por Florentino Pérez y aseguró que estaba centrado en sus proyectos, sin cerrar la puerta a lo que pudiera ocurrir más adelante. Ahora tiene la oportunidad de empezar a trabajar dentro del Madrid. Convertir ese paso en una futura presidencia dependerá de su voluntad en el momento exacto, del respaldo que reúna y del cumplimiento de los requisitos del club. Por ahora, todo encaja...

articles.title: Metrics, Big Cats & Sunday Lunch: What’s Next For Le Bris?
articles.summary: Regis Le Bris has been given the vote of confidence by Sunderland’s hierarchy. But why has it gone so wrong, and can he change it?
articles.body:
Football clubs only let the media know something when they want to.

So when several journalists and aggregator accounts on Twitter spoke of the ownership's plan to back Regis Le Bris, it was a clear statement. Kyril Louis Dreyfus & Co. will reportedly give the Frenchmen time to resolve the club's poor run of form, and potentially provide financial backing in January.

I think there's little value in discussing whether that is the right decision or not, because it's clear the call has been made. Fan sentiment can certainly carry weight with these decisions; just ask Michael Beale, but given the moments and success Le Bris has brought fans on Wearside, there was never going to be a consensus on the Frenchman's future.

What is worth discussing is why Sunderland have struggled so much this season, what Le Bris can do to rectify this, and the wider implications of this call from the ownership.

As I tend to do, I'll try to make sense of on-field matters using numbers, but before that I think there's value in speaking in a less objective manner.

It's clear something doesn't feel right, and I stress the term feel here. For years, lazy pundits, who have shown poor form on both the left and right flanks as well as for England, have used terms like passion or desire when sides are propping up the league table, but to me this doesn't feel apt.

So many of the goals we have seemed to concede have felt like they have been from our own undoing, either from defensive errors or just basic organisational skills. For me, this doesn't ring true with the image of how a Le Bris side operates.

Of course we weren't winning any beauty contests last year, but there was a clear structural foundation that underpinned the way we performed.

If you were to ask me now what has changed, I would use the word assumption. Second-season syndrome is often linked with the idea that a team has been "found out", but in this case I think we have almost found ourselves out.

It feels like it was assumed that when Awoniyi waltzed into the box, a block would come from Alderete or Reinildo. It feels assumed that when we move the ball forward, Brobbey will hold the ball up long enough for the supporting cast to join in. Sadiki can cover a lot of ground, but it feels like his teammates expect him to do the work of ten.

For me, I almost want them to pretend they're strangers and trust in the manager's guidance, but that's just how I feel.

The wider footballing community pretty much had a consensus that Sunderland massively over-performed last season. Whilst I feel this is somewhat reductive, it is worth delving into why this conclusion was made.

What the above graph shows is really interesting. From an xG perspective, Sunderland only came out on top in that battle in 13 of their 38 matches, with only 28.6% of our wins coming with an xG difference of 0.5 or more. We actually won 4 games from games where we would expect to lose more often than not.

Now I don't want to stress the stats too much here; there are several reasons why looking at xG in isolation can be deceptive. We know that a large part of our game last year revolved around being able to absorb pressure, interchanging between a 5-man defense out of possession and a 4-man backline in possession.

Regardless of the discrepancy between where numbers and reality said the Black Cats should've been, one thing is clear. We operated on fine margins last season, I'd argue deliberately so, but fine margins nonetheless.

In its nature, football is a high-variability, low-scoring game. If Trai Hume and O'Nien communicate properly, then the ball never falls to Coventry for their first goal. A slip in wet conditions, the wind in the Leeds game, they ultimately all add up.

There are also a number of immeasurable elements that go into a squad's performance. Let's say we don't get the desired results from Brentford or West Ham early last season. Does the Stadium of Light develop into the fortress it turned to be? Has a larger World Cup taken a slither off of our players' fuel tanks? It certainly looks like Granit Xhaka could've done with his Covid issue being revealed earlier.

Now, in no way am I suggesting that the present downturn in form is down to wind or momentum, but when you operate on a fine margin, then you run the risk of the noise these elements generate on the game having a greater impact on determining which way a result can turn.

There's a reason why the best teams all wish to play with the ball, retaining control of a game. Take a look at Arsenal, my god, they're dull to watch, but they're as much controlling the pitch as they're mitigating the opposition's ability with the ball. It is as much about risk-reduction as it is about attacking dominance.

If Le Bris wants to give his side the best chance of coming out on top in matches, he needs to seek to find a way to reduce the effect "noise" has on our results. That can be done with or without the majority of possession, but the margin for error needs to be mitigated.

What does this mean for Le Bris? Clearly a P45 is not being filled out, but it feels like he has to adapt before it's too late for him. I personally have some concerns as to whether this adaptation could be pushed on him in the guise of a vote of confidence.

When Tony Mowbray left the club, there was a lot of murmuring; he certainly wasn't happy with the level of experience his squad contained, or the sway he had to increase that. There were also rumours going round about the sway and persuasion non-coaching members of staff were giving him regarding squad selection.

Now whilst those rumours were never confirmed, for the sake of a decent article let's assume there was fire along with the smoke.

Le Bris is a conservative and pragmatic manager. What I cannot stress enough is that this is not a criticism; he has got an unbelievable output from our squad and, amongst incredible upheaval, gave me the best Sunderland season I can remember in my 27 years on this earth.

Now if you'll bear with me, I'll tell you about something that is something I'm particular about.

Let's say it's 5pm on a Sunday, I've polished off a roast chicken and a pint of gravy, and I'm ready for a sweet treat. Out comes the apple crumble.

Now, if the crumble is hot, I will require a cold topping (custard, cream, ice cream in order of preference). If the crumble has been sat out and is colder, I'll require a hot topping (most likely custard).

That's just the way I'm wired; I can't change it, and I don't want to change it. Now let's say a man called Glorent Fhisolfi comes out and tells me the custard has to be hot; I'm not sure I'm going to be able to deal with that.

Ultimately, I fear this could be the downfall of Le Bris. You can't ask George Russell to plant a field of barley, and you can't ask Caleb from Clarkson's Farm to take pole at Silverstone. They're both good drivers, but as always, context is key.

Le Bris has had three pre-seasons, countless tactical meetings and daily training sessions to coach his team into the methodology he deems fit for Sunderland. Like it, question it or dislike it, it is a machine of his creation and one which he holds the instruction manual for.

Yes, I want him to play two wingers. Asking our fullbacks to cross the halfway line would massively increase our attacking threat. I'd love Brian Brobbey's hold-up play to be praised far less because I want forwards near him.

But if these changes are to be made under Le Bris, I want them done on his terms.

Why I mentioned Tony Mowbray is because I'm concerned about the precedent any potential pressure on the manager to change his methods may lead to. I hope the confidence they have provided Le Bris with is unconditional, and that any evolution the side undergoes is through his vision.

I have no evidence or reasoning to believe there is pressure from higher up for him to do so, but let's take a look at some facts.

A deadline-day battle for Malick Fofana provided an additional member to an already incredibly deep roster on the left wing at a high price point. Only really in the league cup or the Europa League have we seen two wingers grace the pitch thus far.

Dayann Methalie, a young attacking full-back, was brought in and is yet to see consistent starting minutes in the league. Reinildo hasn't done too much wrong, but it'd be difficult to imagine either man would be given the freedom which would bring out the best of the young French defender.

Clubs like Brentford and Brighton are praised for the structures they put in place. Structures Sunderland have been looking to replicate since KLD took control of the club.

Everyone looks at the transfer turnaround of these clubs, as they rightly should; it's incredible. But what they have done is put structures in place to allow numerous coaches to come in and succeed. Frank to Andrews, Potter to De Zerbi to Hürzeler. Different philosophies, tactics, and methods, but the squad planning was agnostic of this.

Compare this to Manchester United, where Ten Hag brought in his mates from Ajax; Amorim vanquished their wingers, for which he had no need. Carrick is now trying to solve a jigsaw for which he has pieces from Disney's Frozen and English Heritage's Fountains Abbey.

Ghisolfi and Speakman have made finding a replacement for Le Bris simple. The squad has the resources to play a number of different systems, with a number of different options in each position. A significant financial outlay has been made for players which Le Bris is underutilising and potentially could be added to in January.

This is not a criticism of Le Bris, nor is it a criticism of the executive and recruitment teams. It is, however, a concern.

When people want to see a return on their investment in the playing squad, whilst backing the manager, which is mitigating that return, I worry that Le Bris may come under the same pressures that Mowbray reportedly did. Especially when you consider the returns on Ghisolfi's first transfer window are yet to bear fruit, something I'm sure will not be sitting easy with him.

If he succumbs to that pressure, is he capable of that transition? That's something I cannot determine. They say a leopard can't change its spots, but they never say if it has to. Le Bris would be foolish to abandon what has got him this far in his career, but you only have to look at the best managers in recent Premier League history to understand the value of an adaptation to your methods.

Guardiola's centurions often played with a false 9 and a fluid front line. Take a look at the squad he left to Maresca, and physicality appeared to be the primary focus of that side as opposed to technical fluidity. Klopp came in with his "heavy metal football", and departed with a squad that understood the value of control in the Premier League, with physically limited players like Thiago Alcantara shining.

One manager who shouldn't be considered with the two previous is Eddie Howe. I will ask forgiveness for mentioning him, but following his time at Bournemouth, he was conscious enough to know his defensive coaching required work. What did he do? He took time to study under Diego Simeone at Atlético Madrid.

For Le Bris, change is not an admission of defeat or guilt, and has been shown by numerous managers to be beneficial to their success. For better or worse, I only hope he is the driving force behind that change; it is what the man deserves.

articles.title: Sunderland 2-0 Dinamo Zagreb: Black Cats Shocking In First Europa League Defeat
articles.summary: Sunderland fell to a 2-0 defeat against Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday evening.
articles.body:
Sunderland suffer 2-0 Europa League defeat to Dinamo Zagreb

Sunderland suffered their first defeat of the Europa League campaign on Thursday evening as Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb beat the Black Cats 2-0.

On bonfire night, there was a stunning firework display in the intense pre-match atmosphere at the Stadium of Light, but Sunderland's performance during the 90 minutes provided nothing of a sparkle.

Sunderland looked average in the opening exchanges, and midway through the first half, Zagreb took the lead with a volleyed finish from Luka Stojkovic, who caught the ball beautifully after a poor failed clearance from the corner to net the opener.

Despite the technical quality on display with Stojkovic's finish, it begs the question as to why the Dinamo man was unforgivably unmarked by the Sunderland defence at the back post, in a goal eerily similar to the equaliser that the Black Cats conceded in the draw at Lech Poznan in the previous Europa League matchday.

Just moments later, the experienced defensive presence of Thomas Meunier was on hand to thwart an instant advantage doubler, blocking a Zagreb shot off the line for Sunderland as their defensive dishevellment continued.

Meunier was in action once again minutes later, but this time in the Black Cats' final third, hitting the inside of the Zagreb post with a tame effort which proved to be Sunderland's best and only real opening of the half.

Out-of-form Kevin Danso found his way into the referee's book after a foul to halt a Zagreb counterattack courtesy of a poorly weighted pass from the yet again below-par Granit Xhaka, which saw Roefs called into action moments later with a solid stop.
