articles.title: Jaguars are team to beat in the AFC after destroying Ravens to get to 6-2
articles.summary: “Bold City” shook up “Charm City” on Thursday Night Football. The Jacksonville Jaguars forced the Baltimore Ravens to chuck a tabl et and hit new franchise l...
articles.body:
"Bold City" shook up "Charm City" on Thursday Night Football . The Jacksonville Jaguars forced the Baltimore Ravens to chuck a tabl et and hit new franchise lows in the 33-10 rout. But in the process, coach Liam Coen , quarterback Trevor Lawrence and company just put the NFL on notice.

Even in a loaded AFC, the Jags are the new team to beat for these reasons.

Trevor Lawrence is starting to play his best football

Bold statement to make, considering how Lawrence has established himself as a Pro Bowler. But few quarterbacks have created a tear like he has.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"T-Law" hasn't delivered a multiple interception game in his last eight contests. He's also thrown eight touchdowns compared to one pick in his last three games.

Furthermore, the Jaguars have gone 14-3 in their last 17 games with Lawrence behind center. And during that time, he's thrown two or three picks in only two of those contests.

Lawrence currently has thrown 17 touchdowns compared to four aerial takeaways during this start. Coen has unlocked him even further thanks to this pre-snap motion heavy offense featuring play actions and bootlegs, the latter taking advantage of Lawrence's mobility.

Not just limited to a more resurgent Lawrence either.

Wide receiver Parker Washington is averaging 16 yards a catch and leads with four receiving touchdowns. Jakobi Myers has become resurgent in averaging a career-best 14 yards a reception . Then there's leading receiver at tight end in Brenton Strange, who's also hitting a new personal best with 11.9 yards a catch.

All three have surpassed 20 receptions and benefitting from the Los Angeles Rams style attack Coen brought to Duval County. But there's one more fast riser here in running back Bhayshul Tuten. The 2025 fourth rounder owns a combined six touchdowns and has racked up 673 total yards.

Oh, Jacksonville and Coen are starting to involve Travis Hunter both ways too after finally becoming convinced to increase his snaps. But Coen's offense has tallied an astonishing 702 total points through 25 games together.

Hunter is one with two picks on the season to go along with six pass breakups. Fellow cornerback Jourdan Lewis has grabbed two picks too.

Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun adds to the pick party too with his couple of takeaways. But the Jags features nine different defenders who have broken up two to six throws. That includes safety Rayuan Lane III with his four PBUs.

"Bold City" has created a no fly zone under defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile. This will mean names like Patrick Mahomes of the Kansas City Chiefs, Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, even Aaron Rodgers of the Pittsburgh Steelers have a loaded pass defense to deal with should one of them face the Jaguars.

articles.summary: Del 10 al 0, por Juan Ignacio García-Ochoa
articles.body: Fue un visionario al fichar por el Como como jugador y accionista en 2022 y como entrenador lo ha llevado de la Serie B a la mayor goleada de la historia de la Champions. El 1-9 ha puesto definitivamente el foco en el equipo italiano, pero hace tiempo que Cesc Fábregas demuestra que es un elegido de los banquillos. Un 9 para él, porque el 10 es para el nuevo campeón del mundo de Fórmula 1. Campeón del mundo de Fórmula 1 con 20 años. El italiano cerró el título con su tercer puesto en México y batió el récord de precocidad de Vettel. En su segunda temporada ya ha alcanzado lo que muchos persiguen durante toda una carrera. Histórico lo que está haciendo en el Como. Llegó como futbolista en 2022, se convirtió en accionista, cogió el equipo en segunda como técnico y lo ascendió a la Serie A en 2024. En 2026 ya está en la Champions, en el top 8 y con la mayor goleada de la historia. Se estrenó en la distancia del maratón ganando en Nueva York, que celebró su 50 edición. El sueco se impuso en 2:06:01 y añadió otro gran éxito a su temporada. Además, es el primer atleta nacido en Europa que gana desde 1996, rompiendo con un asfixiante dominio africano de 30 años. Brillante su movimiento con Rafa Nadal, consiguiendo que uno de los mejores atletas de la historia se una a la marca más importante del deporte. Un golpe planetario. Imposible que el madridismo no sueñe con Rafa como presidente cuando Florentino decida echarse a un lado. La mejor decisión posible por parte del Real Madrid. Carlos sacó adelante su estreno en París ante Michelsen y accedió directamente a cuartos tras la baja por lesión de Berrettini. El pase de ayer llegó sin jugar, pero el trabajo previo estaba hecho y en París estamos viendo a un Carlitos optimista y feliz en la pista. Alcaraz ha olvidado sus problemas físicos y sigue en carrera por el último Masters 1.000 del año. Plagado de bajas, el Real Madrid llevó al Panathinaikos hasta la prórroga en la Euroliga, pero acabó perdiendo por 112-115 en casa. Hubo muchísimo esfuerzo y capacidad para competir, pero también errores que un rival de este nivel castiga. Pese a todo, una heroicidad teniendo en cuento cómo llegaba el equipo. El domingo tiene una oportunidad de oro para dar un golpe encima de la mesa de LaLiga, pero el bajonazo en la Champions es importante. Solo cuatro puntos y una derrota ante el Bayern de las que dejan dudas... Otra lesión que le deja KO. Yen este caso, además, le deja fuera de la Conference League, ya que el Mónaco ha decidido darle la baja. Las lesiones, su gran lastre. Los dos coches abandonaron en México tras apenas seis vueltas. El domingo de la coronación de Antonelli dejó a Alonso sin posibilidad siquiera de pelear por un resultado. Para olvidar. El 0-6 ante el PSG en casa fue el golpe más duro de la jornada europea para los equipos españoles. El nivel del adversario explica la dificultad del partido, pero una diferencia así obliga a revisar mucho más que los errores puntuales. Pese al duro golpe, debería mantener la calma al Villarreal y seguir confiando en un entrenador como Iñigo Pérez, que seguro que acaba dando con la tecla. El LIV Golf desaparece después de que BC Partners haya retirado los 300 millones de dólares con los que pretendía rescatar el circuito saudí. La marcha de estrellas como Jon Rahm y Sergio García ha terminado de hundir un proyecto que nació para revolucionar el golf mundial y que, apenas cuatro años después de su estreno, se enfrenta a su liquidación tras acumular pérdidas multimillonarias. articles.title: Wayne Rooney: Former Man Utd and England captain named pundit of year
articles.summary: Former Manchester United and England captain Wayne Rooney is named pundit of the year at the prestigious Broadcast Sport Awards.
articles.body:
"I like a lot of them artists, but I thought it was crap."

Wayne Rooney's assessment of the 2026 World Cup final half-time show - delivered live on BBC Television - was blunt.

The show, which featured Madonna, BTS, Shakira and Justin Bieber, ran to 27 minutes and 22 seconds. Rooney, who played at three World Cups for England, was unimpressed.

It caught some - including fellow pundit Joe Hart - by surprise. But Rooney's plain-speaking and sense of humour through the tournament had connected with viewers.

On Thursday, the former Manchester United and England captain was named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards. , external

Rooney, 41, was presented with the prestigious prize in front of 650 people from the sports television industry at a ceremony in London.

"I didn't realise how tough it was going to be when I first started doing it," said Rooney about transitioning from football to broadcasting.

"I've always been my own biggest critic. And even now I need to improve, I need to be better.

Rooney's move to broadcasting after a stellar playing career - followed by a testing stint as a manager - has not always been smooth.

His debut as a full-time pundit on Match of the Day in August 2025 divided opinion, , external with one fan writing on social media: "Just because you have done something, does not automatically make you good to talk/explain and teach others well."

Guardian journalist Paul MacInnes was more upbeat about Rooney's debut.

"He's articulate, and on Saturday night was able to conjure up the right word when you could see he was looking for it," he wrote. , external

"He is tactically insightful and has a wealth of experience to draw from too."

As a player, Rooney learned from managers including Sir Alex Ferguson and David Moyes, and won the Champions League, Europa League, Premier League (five times), FA Cup and League Cup (three times).

He was not always the most articulate in his post-match interviews. As a pundit, he has found his voice.

In an attempt to better himself as a broadcaster, Rooney has sought feedback and advice from experienced television executives, as well as other players-turned-pundits including Alan Shearer, Danny Murphy, Hart and Micah Richards.

"I do look at the other pundits who have been there a long time," added Rooney.

"I see how they do it. I enjoy it, it keeps me involved in football."

Asked about dealing with criticism from people watching him on TV, Rooney responded: "You do see it.

"It drives me to be better. I always feel when I do something I want to do better and be the best I can."

Paul Stretford, Rooney's long-serving agent, said people should not be surprised by what his client can achieve.

"It is no surprise to me that Wayne has continued to put his doubters in their place with his football intelligence and straightforward manner," added Stretford.

"Time and time again as a player he was able to raise his game to incredible levels.

"They should also not be surprised at his drive and ambition to be the best that he can possibly be. And he does this with a combination of intelligence and humility."

Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Rooney had shown a "great willingness to learn and determination to improve" as a broadcaster.

"Wayne is also a very likeable guy, a proper team player, with no ego on display," he added.

As well as developing chemistry with his fellow pundits, Rooney has changed his appearance after committing to a healthier lifestyle through a fitness regime which involves games of padel and boxing training.

"Like anyone who cares about their job, Wayne had to work hard - to learn skills around analysis and delivery - and he's improved so much in a short time," said Alex Kay-Jelski, director of BBC Sport.

"Micah and Joe alongside him at the World Cup were perfect team-mates - three equals - and you'll be seeing more of them together on the BBC in coming seasons."

Their chemistry was obvious in the summer, particularly when they swapped their microphones for oars after an erroneous Rooney prediction.

He pledged to row down the River Mersey if Norway beat Brazil, and when they did, he confirmed on air he would adapt the challenge to do it in the United States.

That led to him, Hart and Richards to take to the Hudson River in New York.

"Wayne deserves this so much," added Kay-Jelski. "He's a great mix of incredibly clever, funny in a self-deprecating manner and likeable.

"From a BBC side he's easy to work with, treats everyone the same whether they're a former team-mate or starting out in a junior position, and his words carry real weight."

articles.title: Spanish media fawns over Bayern Munich’s 2-0 win over Atletico Madrid
articles.summary: FC Bayern had the press of an entirely different nation raving over them
articles.body:
Bayern Munich won 2-0 and completely shut out Atlético Madrid in the Champions League. It was a much-needed win for the Bavarians, which boosts their chances of finishing in the top eight. Conversely, it damages Atleti's chances of a top-eight finish. The magnitude of the win was big enough that numerous Spanish news outlets collectively ran out of superlatives to describe Bayern's performance (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ):

Bayern were a steamroller – both in terms of footballing quality and determination, they were simply too much for Atlético to handle. Bayern were by far the best team to visit the Metropolitano this year. Pure elite.

A magnificent team conquers the Metropolitano. The Germans seemed to be playing an entirely different game: faster, sharper, more physical. Relentless. Giants playing against children.

A depleted Bayern Munich bring Atlético back down to earth. The Bavarians completely overwhelmed Atlético Madrid, who had gone nine consecutive games unbeaten.

Bayern overpower Atlético and hold up a mirror to them. A perfectly oiled machine that Atlético simply could not cope with.

This defeat put a massive dent in Atleti's hopes of qualifying as a seeded team (or top eight) while it simultaneously boosted Bayern's chances of finishing higher than ninth place.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City (Premier League): Match Preview, Team News, Head to Head, How to Watch
articles.summary: Midweek UEFA Champions League action saw Enzo Maresca's side pick up their first non-penalty shootout win since October 20, with a fifth win from seven match...
articles.body:
Midweek UEFA Champions League action saw Enzo Maresca's side pick up their first non-penalty shootout win since October 20, with a fifth win from seven matches against RB Leipzig.

Despite a largley uninspiring performance in the first-half, the Blues took the lead in the 37th minute in a lightning fast exchange, kick-started by Rayan Cherki.

The France international's long ball was inch-perfect, finding the feet of Nico O'Reilly, from there the fullback drilled it into the box in search of Enzo Fernandez. While he didn't reach the intended target, a clumsy block from Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba saw the ball bundled into the back of the net, giving the visitors the lead.

Into the second-half, Manchester City still struggled to gain a foothold into the match. Moments after making a sensational save, an error from Gianluigi Donnarumma saw the ball nestling in the back of the net. What looked like a cross from Ridle Baku had crept in at the inside post, leaving Maresca's side with it all to do just after the break.

Just 10 minutes later, Fernandez stepped up to give his side the lead once more. Iliman Ndiaye's in-swinging cross was met by a bullet header from the Argentine, and Manchester City looked to be heading home with all three points once again.

But, once again the hosts came up with an equaliser. Christopher Nkunku's pass cleared the City back four, laying perfectly in the path of Antonio Nusa who made no mistake. The Norwegian winger showing exactly why he has become so highly sought after, giving his side a lifeline.

Still, the visitors struggled to really take hold of the match. Former Nottingham Forest man Elliot Anderson has very quickly become a fan favourite in his brief time at the Etihad, and his work for the winner served as an example of exactly what he is capable of.

Springing forward from the midfield, Anderson carried the ball out wide before wrapping his foot around the ball to unleash the perfect cross towards the back post. From there, who else but Erling Haaland to finish it off?

With all three points confirmed, up next for Manchester City is a trip to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest.

Forest enter this one amid an incredibly poor run of form, with just one win since the start of the season. They currently sit second from the bottom, with only Regis Le Bris' Sunderland having a worse start to the season. Despite their poor run of form, even just a point could see them end the weekend ahead of Manchester United .

City's recent league form leaves a lot to be desired too though, with two losses from the last two, a win here is imperative in order to keep within touching distance of leaders Arsenal . It may still be early on in the title race, but going six points behind at this stage could prove very difficult to come back from.

In recent fixtures, matchups against Forest have been anything but straight forward, but given their struggles since losing star midfielder Anderson, you would be forgiven for thinking that this one should be that little bit easier.

Here is everything you need to know ahead of Manchester City 's Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest!

Nottingham Forest will host Manchester City at the City Ground on Saturday 7 November, with kick-off scheduled for 17:30 UK.

Yorkshireman Sam Barrott has been appointed referee ahead of Saturday's fixture.

Barrott's last time refereeing a City match was the 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal. In total, he has refereed seven Manchester City matches, with four wins for the Blues and three defeats.

You can find the full list of match officials below!

For Manchester City, only Antoine Semenyo misses out. The winger is expected to return shortly before the end of the year.

Oliver Glasner will be without Nicolo Savona , Nicolas Dominguez and Igor Jesus .

Savona has been out of action since January with a knee injury, while he has returned to training, this one will come too soon for him.

Dominguez picked up a knock in the recent 1-0 defeat to Arsenal and is unlikely to feature on Saturday.

Igor Jesus has been sidelined with a calf injury since September, following his side's 0-1 defeat to Coventry City.

Enzo Maresca will preview the trip to Forest in a press conference at the City Football Academy from 13:30 UK on Friday.

Manchester City have faced Nottingham Forest 109 times since 1899, in that time the Blues have won 46 times and lost on 34 occasions.

Since Forest's return to the top flight in 2022, City have taken all three points from six of the nine meetings. Forest's sole win from those nine occasions came in the 2024-25 season, when Callum Hudson-Odoi's 83rd minute effort was enough to seal the win.

Last time out, it was Elliot Anderson who put a nail in the coffin of City's title aspirations with a long-range equaliser. On that day, Antoine Semenyo opened the scoring with Rodri cancelling out Morgan Gibbs-White's initial equaliser, it was then that Anderson struck to rain on City's parade.

In the fixture before that, goals from Rayan Cherki and Tijjani Reijnders were enough to provide City with a 2-1 comeback triumph.

Nottingham Forest are joint last in the scoring charts, with just six goals so far this season. For reference, Erling Haaland currently sits on nine goals in the league.

Forest have failed to score in five of their nine outings in the league this season, also failing to score in the opening round of the Carabao Cup.

A goal for Erling Haaland would see him become joint top scorer in this fixture, with Niall Quinn having scored six against Forest in his time at the club.

The Norwegian striker has failed to score in his last four appearances against Forest, a rare blank streak by his standards.

Oliver Glasner's side are yet to score a goal at home this season, their longest goal drought at home since 2018, where they failed to score across six consecutive home games.

Manchester City have not lost three consecutive Premier League matches since Manuel Pellegrini was in charge, with the last time being back in March 2016.

Oliver Glasner has failed to win any of his five previous Premier League meetings with City as a manager, losing four and drawing one during his time at Crystal Palace . His sides conceded at least three goals in all four defeats.

Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City will be available to watch on Sky Sports Main Event, for those watching in the UK. Radio coverage will be available on BBC Radio 5 Live .

articles.title: FA Cup: From facing Lionel Messi & Cristiano Ronaldo to non-league for Fernando Forestieri
articles.summary: Fernando Forestieri, whose career has seen him play against Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, is looking to inspire non-league Oxford City to a memorable FA Cup win over Leicester City.
articles.body:
A Saturday afternoon in October at the Hebburn Sports and Social Ground, Tyne & Wear.

Some Hebburn Town fans are already heading for the exits as Oxford City, 3-0 up in the 81st minute, send on their new signing.

Fernando Forestieri has shared pitches with Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Zlatan Ibrahimovic, and played in front 72,000 fans at Real Madrid's iconic Bernabeu Stadium.

On this occasion, in English football's sixth tier, there are 873 supporters present to witness Oxford City's new Argentine number 15 come on for his debut.

"It was like a tennis match, the ball going one way one second, then the other way the next," Forestieri, 36, told BBC Sport after his new club, nicknamed the Hoops, secured a seventh win in 11 games to sit third in National League North.

On Friday, Oxford City host Leicester City in the first round of the FA Cup (19:45 GMT), with former Watford and Sheffield Wednesday forward Forestieri looking to inspire the non-league club to a famous win over the League One Foxes.

It is 10 years since Leicester famously won the Premier League title. In the same season Forestieri was helping Sheffield Wednesday reach the Championship play-off final, where the Owls lost to Hull City at Wembley.

"There's a big gap between what Leicester did 10 years ago and where they are now," he said.

"Why can't Oxford City cause an upset? This is what the FA Cup is all about."

Forestieri ready for fresh challenge at Oxford City

Forestieri encountered Barcelona, Messi and Ibrahimovic while playing for Malaga in Spain's top flight in 2009-10.

Meanwhile, he shared the same pitch with Ronaldo as recently as five years ago when Juventus played Forestieri's Udinese team in Serie A.

"You never forget being on the same pitch as these big players," added Forestieri, whose CV includes scoring against Inter Milan for Siena.

"Messi, Ronaldo, Ibrahimovic... unbelievable skills.

"I'm very lucky. Being that close to them you remember their first touch, their vision."

Forestieri grew up playing football on the streets of Rosario - the same city in Argentina Messi was born - and idolised Diego Maradona.

When Maradona died in 2020, Forestieri wrote a tribute to the 1986 Argentina World Cup winner on the back of his Udinese shirt.

"Growing up in Argentina, everyone pretended to be Diego," he said.

"He was a hero to everyone. On every corner of every street someone painted his face on a wall."

Talking about his childhood, Forestieri said: "I was born poor, born with nothing.

"I lived with my mum and dad and two brothers. The five of us slept in one room."

Rosario was a dangerous area and Forestieri's brother, Maximiliano, was shot and wounded.

"Thankfully he survived," said Forestieri, who was part of the academies of famed Argentine clubs Newell's Old Boys and Boca Juniors.

Aged 16, he moved to Italy and quickly made his senior debut for Genoa.

He qualified to play for Italy through his grandfather and turned out for the Azzurri at youth levels.

Twenty years after his senior debut for Genoa, and after recent spells in Malaysia and Cyprus, he is still playing - albeit in non-league, after returning to England following the birth of his third son, Luciano.

So, how did his move to Oxford City come about?

Forestieri was at Watford at the same time as Hoops boss Ross Jenkins, while Oxford City assistant manager Paul Robinson is also a former Hornets player.

He trained with the PFA as part of their pre-season programme for players without a club before getting a call from Robinson.

"Robbo said: 'why you don't come here to help us? We'll help you to become fit'," explained Forestieri.

"For me this is a big change. But I'm so happy to be at Oxford City. They are an ambitious club and I want to help them as much as I can."

The player, who is also taking his coaching badges, lives in north London with his wife, Andria, and their two other sons Santiago, aged nine, and Maximiliano, aged six.

"I still have passion for football," he added.

"Whenever I'm walking in the park with Santiago and we see someone playing football, we stop and join in. That's how much I still love football."

After the money-spinning Leicester tie, which is expected to attract a 3,500 sell-out crowd, Oxford City make the long journey to the north-east to play Darlington in a league match next Tuesday.

"You need to listen to your body when you reach 36," said Forestieri.

"But I'm lucky to be still playing and that a club still wants me to play for them."

articles.title: La cuenta pendiente de Flick con Simeone
articles.standfirst: El argentino es el técnico al que más veces se ha enfrentado el alemán
articles.summary: El argentino es el técnico al que más veces se ha enfrentado el alemán
articles.body: Para Hansi Flick, medirse a Diego Pablo Simeone se ha convertido prácticamente en una costumbre. El técnico argentino es el entrenador al que más veces se ha enfrentado desde que inició su trayectoria en los banquillos. Tanto durante su etapa al frente del Bayern de Múnich como ahora como entrenador del Barcelona, el alemán se ha cruzado con el Atlético de Madrid en 12 ocasiones. Un historial en el que, por el momento, el azulgrana lleva la delantera en número de victorias. Sin embargo, Simeone ha conseguido asestarle dos golpes especialmente dolorosos durante la pasada temporada, al eliminar al conjunto catalán tanto de la Copa del Rey como de la Champions League. Dos eliminaciones que todavía representan una espina clavada para Flick. La historia de esta particular rivalidad comenzó hace ya seis años. Flick y Simeone se enfrentaron por primera vez un 21 de octubre de 2020, en la primera jornada de la fase de grupos de la Champions League. Aquel encuentro, disputado en el Allianz Arena, terminó con una contundente victoria del Bayern de Múnich por 4-0 contra el conjunto rojiblanco. El equipo alemán, dirigido entonces por Flick, dejó patente su superioridad y abrió una serie de enfrentamientos que, con el paso del tiempo, se han convertido en casi una tradición. Desde entonces, ambos entrenadores han vuelto a encontrarse en numerosas ocasiones, aunque la mayoría de los duelos han llegado con Flick ya al frente del Barcelona. De los 12 enfrentamientos disputados, 10 se han producido durante su etapa en el banquillo azulgrana. En ese periodo, el balance del alemán contra el Atlético de Simeone es de seis victorias, un empate y tres derrotas. Unos números que reflejan cierta superioridad culé, aunque las estadísticas no cuentan toda la historia. Y es que dos de esas derrotas tuvieron consecuencias especialmente importantes para el Barcelona. La primera llegó en la ida de las semifinales de la Copa del Rey, cuando el Atlético firmó un contundente 4-0 que dejó a los azulgranas virtualmente eliminados del torneo del K.O. La segunda fue todavía más dolorosa por el escenario y la competición: el conjunto rojiblanco se impuso por 0-2 en el partido de ida de los cuartos de final de la Champions League, disputado en el Spotify Camp Nou. Un resultado que obligó a los de Flick a buscar una remontada en el Metropolitano que finalmente no pudo materializarse. Simeone ha demostrado que, pese a partir en ocasiones con menos protagonismo en las quinielas, ha conseguido convertir los enfrentamientos directos contra el Barcelona de Flick en una prueba de máxima exigencia para el entrenador alemán, especialmente cuando hay un título o una eliminatoria europea en juego. Hay, además, un dato que define bastante bien el carácter de esta rivalidad: los partidos entre ambos nunca han terminado con un 0-0. En ninguno de los 12 enfrentamientos se ha cerrado el marcador sin goles y solo una vez se resolvió por un solitario 0-1. Dos estilos diferentes, dos entrenadores con personalidades muy marcadas y una rivalidad que ha ido creciendo con el paso de las temporadas.

articles.title: Who is Kozo Tashima, the Japanese official running for FIFA presidency?
articles.summary: Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat, and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands.
articles.body:
Kozo Tashima first started playing football after watching the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and since then he has dedicated his life to developing the sport’s growth in Japan.

The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino in football’s governing body’s election in March.

Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands.

He rarely makes headlines, and one of the few times he appeared outside the sport pages was when he became one of the first public figures in Japan to contract coronavirus in March 2020.

He spent time studying at the German Sport University Cologne and said the experience changed the way he saw sport’s purpose in society.

He says his decision to run for the FIFA presidency was based on a belief that “in this age of business and money, sport must firmly uphold its integrity”.

“The worst thing would be if he [Infantino] were to continue without an election,” he told reporters after announcing his candidacy.

“I feel this is a test of whether FIFA has the ability to cleanse itself.”

Tashima was born in southern Kumamoto and captained his team to the title in Japan’s prestigious national high school championship.

With no professional football in the country at the time, he had ambitions of becoming a PE teacher and enrolled at a university, where he was called up to play for Japan’s full national team.

He joined a club in Japan’s amateur league after graduating but soon retired as a player and went to Germany to study to become a coach.

He described his “profound shock” at the players’ superior skills and the way football was viewed there.

“Even back in 1980, the training in Germany was hugely scientific and systematic,” he said.

“Everything seemed like a different world from Japan, and it was a big culture shock for me.”

Tashima returned home determined to use what he had learned in Germany and help develop Japanese football.

He coached a university team before joining the Japan Football Association (JFA), where he worked on development programmes and coached the country’s national teams at various youth levels.

He rose through the JFA ranks and was elected president in 2016, while also serving on the Asian Football Confederation executive committee and the FIFA Council.

His reign as JFA chief saw him fire Japan coach Vahid Halilhodzic two months before the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

Halilhodzic, who was unpopular with the players, was replaced by Akira Nishino, and Japan reached the last 16, where they were eliminated by Belgium.

“Some people told me that I wasn’t the one who hired Halilhodzic so it wouldn’t be my fault if the team lost,” Tashima said.

“But as president, all the responsibility lay with me.”

Tashima stepped down as JFA chief in 2024 and was named honorary president.

He said he had decided to run for the FIFA presidency to “contribute to the further development of world football”.

Tashima said he was troubled by FIFA’s shock decision to lift a ban for United States player Folarin Balogun at this year’s World Cup, following an intervention by US President Donald Trump .

He said he also had a problem with the travel restrictions placed on Iran’s World Cup team by American authorities.

Tashima, who has the JFA’s backing, said his presidency bid was “not about winning or losing”.

“What matters is sharing with the world the integrity that Japan’s football has built over the years,” he said.
